ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.5m. It is olive-brown with dark, pale-edged longitudinal stripes. Key features include a pointed snout and large, round eyes with round pupils. Family: Psammophiidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature for *Psammophis condanarus* is the presence of a distinct, broad dark vertebral stripe bordered by two thinner, pale longitudinal lines.
ai.habitat: *Psammophis condanarus* inhabits dry, open grasslands, scrub forests, and agricultural fields in the Indian plains, typically below an altitude of 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The striped sand snake is primarily diurnal, actively hunting lizards and small rodents by pursuing them across open, arid terrain with impressive speed.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammophis condanarus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–11 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August) in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Psammophis condanarus* occurs across the Indo-Gangetic plains and central India, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,500 meters in the Himalayan foothills.
